Working plan from today (Aug 25) to the results freeze in December.
The [top-level Gantt](../../index.qmd) is the source of truth for
dates; this page holds the reasoning behind them: research questions,
week-level milestones, the quantifiables spec (metrics, generalization
tiers, failure taxonomy), the literature map, the open-source stack,
and how AI research assistants are used. Revise it whenever the plan
changes — it becomes the skeleton of the Methods chapter and the
defense timeline slide.

## Research questions

The thesis claim is built around three questions. Every experiment
should answer one of them; anything that doesn't is scope creep.

**RQ1 — Adaptation.** Can current open vision-language-action (VLA)
foundation models (NVIDIA GR00T N1.5, SmolVLA, optionally π0) be
adapted to a *new embodiment* — the OARbot (Clearpath Dingo omni base
+ Kinova Jaco Gen2 6-DOF arm) — with a modest demonstration dataset
collected in the lab?

**RQ2 — Comparison & generalization.** On a fixed task suite, how do
the fine-tuned VLAs compare against each other *and against a
from-scratch imitation baseline (ACT) trained only on our
demonstrations* — both on in-distribution success rate and on how
gracefully performance degrades across generalization tiers (unseen
poses, distractors, novel object instances, paraphrased
instructions)? The baseline is what makes generalization attributable:
if the VLAs degrade less than ACT out of distribution, that gap *is*
the measured value of internet-scale pretraining.

**RQ3 — Practicality.** What are the real compute and data costs —
fine-tuning wall-clock on a DGX Spark, demos-per-task needed, on-robot
inference rates — and what does that imply for small-lab replication?

RQ3 is the differentiator: most VLA papers report results on the
authors' hardware fleet; a careful account of what it takes to adapt
these models on one robot with two lab machines is a genuine
contribution.

## Compute and platform allocation

| Machine | Role |
|---|---|
| DGX Spark (GB10, 128 GB unified memory) | All fine-tuning: GR00T N1.5 (NVIDIA ships a DGX Spark fine-tuning playbook for it), SmolVLA full fine-tune, π0 LoRA if attempted |
| RTX workstation ("7080" — confirm exact model, likely RTX 5080) | Policy inference at eval time (joins the robot's ROS 2 graph over the network), dataset QC and visualization |
| OARbot's own computers | Teleop and demo recording happen here, not on the RTX box: Surface Go 2 tablet + SpaceMouse/deadman/E-stop is the operator interface; the **helper laptop** is the hub that drives the Kinova arm (USB-B) and runs the device nodes; the Dingo onboard PC runs the ROS 2 Jazzy base; the NUC handles overhead-camera pose estimation (per the [OARbot docs](https://rpirobotics.github.io/oarbots/docs/getting-started/hardware-overview)) |

Keep training and robot operation on separate machines from day one so
data collection never competes with training runs.

## Month-by-month plan

### September — bring-up, task suite, literature (epics B1, A2, A1)

- **Week of Sep 1:** Full teleop chain on one OARbot: drive the base,
  command the arm (SpaceMouse), stream both Azure Kinects. Verify
  E-stop and deadman behavior. Note which sensors are actually usable
  (docs already flag the UWB units as inoperable).
- **Week of Sep 8:** Record demonstrations into **LeRobotDataset
  format** — joint states + base velocity + camera frames, replay a
  recorded episode open-loop on the robot to prove the pipeline is
  lossless. This replay test is the single most important de-risking
  step of the semester.
- **Week of Sep 15:** Freeze the **task suite** (epic A2): 3 tasks in
  increasing difficulty, e.g. (T1) tabletop pick-and-place, arm only;
  (T2) fetch — navigate to a table, grasp, return; (T3) a true
  mobile-manipulation task with base+arm coordination (open a door,
  clear a table). Scope grows in that order **by design**: start
  arm-only with the base parked, expand only once T1 works. Even so,
  freeze the full 10-D action/state schema (6 arm + 3 base + gripper)
  from the first recorded episode — base dims logged as zeros while
  parked — so widening scope later means new data, never a pipeline
  rewrite. Define per-task success criteria, the staged
  **progress rubric** (reach / grasp / transport / place), the
  in-distribution randomization grid, and the **generalization tiers
  G1–G4** (see the quantifiables spec below) *before* collecting
  data. Confirm the suite with the advisor. Also start the
  **action-space decision log**: every embodiment-design choice
  (joint deltas vs. absolutes, base twist representation, chunk
  length, control rates, normalization) gets a dated entry with the
  reasoning — this log becomes the Methods section on adapting VLA
  action heads to a mobile manipulator.
- **Week of Sep 22:** Pilot data collection: ~10 episodes per task,
  train a quick SmolVLA sanity run on T1, fix whatever breaks.
- **Gate 1 (Sep 26):** teleop + record + replay all work, task suite
  signed off. *Fallback if late: drop T3 base motion and run an
  arm-centric thesis — decide here, not in November.*

#### Data-pipeline decisions (locked 2026-08-25)

- Teleop is **Cartesian** (SpaceMouse → EE twist → Kinova IK);
  training actions are **joint positions** derived from achieved
  states: action(t) = joint angles at t+Δ. Teleop space and training
  space are decoupled by this labeling — the raw SpaceMouse commands
  are never used as labels.
- Recording = `ros2 bag record` on the **helper laptop** (compressed
  image topics, one auto-numbered bag per episode), then an offline
  **bag → LeRobotDataset converter**: uniform rate, nearest-frame
  alignment, the frozen 10-D schema, t+Δ action labels, instruction
  string per episode. Raw bags are kept forever as source of truth —
  every labeling choice stays reversible without re-collection.
- **Wrist camera mounted before any kept demos** — observations are
  locked in at recording time; actions can be re-derived, images
  cannot.

#### Week-1 verification checklist (at the robot)

1. `ros2 topic list` + `ros2 topic hz` during teleop: arm JointState
   topic (finger joints included?), camera topics, `/odom`, raw
   teleop command topic if exposed. Note exact names and rates.
2. **Angular control** — does the lab stack expose joint
   position/velocity *streaming* to the Gen2? Teleop only proves the
   Cartesian path; policies need the joint path. Biggest unknown on
   the platform.
3. Gripper commands land on a ROS topic and appear in recordings.
4. Round-trip latency: camera → RTX box → command back to the helper
   laptop (decides wireless inference viability; chunk ≈ 3× latency).
5. Clock sync (chrony) across Dingo PC / helper laptop / NUC / RTX
   box — required for correct chunk alignment at deployment.
6. End-to-end proof: record one episode → convert → **replay** it on
   the arm via angular control.

### October — dataset at scale + first baseline (epics B2, C2)

- **Weeks of Oct 5 / Oct 12:** Main collection push, target **50–100
  episodes per task** (ACT/SmolVLA-class results are routinely
  reported around 50 demos/task; more helps T3). Interleave tasks and
  vary object poses per the randomization grid. Nightly QC script:
  episode counts, joint-limit outliers, dropped frames.
- **Week of Oct 19:** SmolVLA fine-tuned per-task on the Spark, and
  **ACT trained from scratch on the identical data** — it trains in
  hours and rides along on the same LeRobot dataset, giving the
  no-pretraining reference point for RQ2. First closed-loop rollouts
  on the robot.
- **Week of Oct 26:** Start GR00T N1.5 fine-tuning (epic C1) — the
  new-embodiment head needs the most debugging lead time. First
  structured mini-eval (10 trials/task) of SmolVLA.
- **Gate 2 (Oct 31):** SmolVLA achieves non-zero success on T1 with a
  documented eval protocol. *If zero: freeze collection, debug the
  data/normalization/camera pipeline first — more bad data won't
  help.*

### November — GR00T + full evaluation (epics C1, C3)

- **Weeks of Nov 2 / Nov 9:** GR00T N1.5 tuned across tasks; top-up
  data collection where QC shows gaps; π0 (LoRA via LeRobot/openpi)
  only if both main models are stable.
- **Week of Nov 16:** Full evaluation begins (epic C3): **≥20
  trials/task/policy** on the shared in-distribution grid, everything
  in the quantifiables spec logged per trial, video of every trial.
  Budget realistically — 3 tasks × 4 policies (ACT, SmolVLA, GR00T,
  π0-if-attempted) × 20 trials at ~3 min/trial is ~12 robot-hours
  *per full round*, plus resets.
- **Gate 3 (Nov 27):** Decide final comparison set (ACT + 2 or 3
  VLAs) and confirm the **data-scale ablation** (retrain at 25/50/100
  demos on one task) fits the calendar.

### December — finish, freeze, outline (epics C3, D)

- **Weeks of Dec 1 / Dec 7:** Complete in-distribution eval rounds +
  data-scale ablation; **generalization round** — tiers G1–G4 on each
  model's best checkpoint only (10 trials/tier, see quantifiables
  spec).
- **Week of Dec 14:** Re-runs and holes only. **Results freeze Dec 18**
  — after this date, no new experiments, only analysis.
- **Week of Dec 21:** All results tables and figures generated by
  script from logged data; chapter outline drafted in `chapters/`.

### January–March 2027

Chapter drafts Jan 4 – Feb 26 (Background and Methods first — most of
Methods should fall out of this page and the epic READMEs), full draft
to advisor end of February, defense mid-March (confirm the exact date
and committee logistics with the advisor **in September**, not
January).

## Quantifiables — what gets measured and reported

What the results chapter must contain, modeled on what this class of
papers (ACT, Diffusion Policy, OpenVLA, π0, SmolVLA, GR00T, Mobile
ALOHA) actually reports. Frozen in epic A2 before data collection;
every eval trial logs a row with all of these fields plus a video
path.

### Decision thresholds — what "achieved" means

Targets are pre-registered thresholds, not promises. A miss, analyzed
honestly, is still a result.

- **Platform validated:** ≥1 policy reaches **≥70% success on T1**
  in-distribution.
- **Pretraining transfer confirmed:** the VLAs beat from-scratch ACT
  on the generalization tiers by **≥15 percentage points** average. A
  null or negative gap = "pretraining did not pay off at this data
  scale on this embodiment" — a publishable negative result.
- **Practicality documented:** complete cost sheet (below) for every
  model, no gaps.

### Primary metrics (every policy, every task)

| Metric | Definition | Reported as |
|---|---|---|
| Success rate | Binary per trial against the frozen rubric; human intervention = failure | % with 95% Wilson CI, n ≥ 20 |
| Progress score | Staged credit: reach 0.25 / grasp 0.5 / transport 0.75 / place 1.0 (per-task rubric) | Mean 0–1; separates "never grasps" from "drops at the end" when success rates are low |
| Time to completion | Successful trials only, start signal → success condition | Median [IQR] seconds |

### Secondary metrics

| Metric | Definition | Reported as |
|---|---|---|
| Inference latency | Camera frame in → action chunk out, on the RTX workstation | ms per chunk + achieved control rate (Hz) |
| Generalization gap | In-distribution success minus per-tier success | Percentage points, per tier per policy |
| Data efficiency | Success rate at 25 / 50 / 100 training demos (one task, all policies) | Curve — the small-lab money figure |

### Generalization tiers (RQ2)

Evaluated on each model's **best checkpoint only**, 10 trials/tier,
selection rules frozen in A2:

- **G0** — in-distribution: objects and poses from the training grid.
- **G1 — spatial:** object poses outside the training grid.
- **G2 — visual:** distractor objects + lighting change.
- **G3 — object:** novel instance of the same category (different
  mug, different box).
- **G4 — language:** paraphrased instruction, same task ("pick up the
  cup" → "grab the mug"). VLA-only tier — ACT has no language input,
  which is itself part of the comparison story.

### Failure taxonomy

Every failed trial gets a **first-failure label** from this closed
list, logged at eval time (10 seconds of effort) with the video path:

`perception/grounding` (approached wrong object) ·
`navigation/base-pose` (stopped out of reach) · `grasp` (contact but
slip/miss) · `manipulation-trajectory` (jerky/unsafe motion, joint
limit) · `instruction` (did the wrong task) · `stall/timeout` ·
`hardware` (excluded and retried, not counted).

Rendered as stacked bars per policy × task — this figure explains
*why* the success rates differ and is the backbone of the analysis
chapter.

### Practicality cost sheet (RQ3)

Per model: fine-tuning wall-clock hours and peak memory on the DGX
Spark, trainable parameter count (LoRA vs. full), GPU-hours per
training run, on-robot inference hardware requirements. Plus data
cost: minutes per collected episode, total collection hours, retake
rate.

### Deliverables checklist (results chapter)

- **T1** Main results: success ± CI, task × policy, in-distribution
- **T2** Generalization matrix: policy × tier
- **T3** Efficiency: latency, control rate, completion time
- **T4** Cost sheet (RQ3)
- **F1** Data-scale curve · **F2** Failure-mode stacked bars ·
  **F3** Qualitative rollout film-strips (best + worst per policy)

Protocol hygiene: the randomization grid and rubrics are frozen
before collection; checkpoint selection criteria defined before eval;
all runs reported (no cherry-picked seeds); every trial has video.

## Literature map

Organized by the Background chapter's likely sections. Maintain
citations in Zotero and export to `references.bib` (keep BibTeX keys
stable). Verify every reference on arXiv/Semantic Scholar before it
enters the bib file — never cite from an LLM's memory.

**1. Learning from demonstration — foundations**

- Argall, Chernova, Veloso, Browning (2009), *A survey of robot
  learning from demonstration* — the canonical survey to anchor the
  chapter.
- Pomerleau (1988), ALVINN — behavioral cloning origin.
- Ross, Gordon, Bagnell (2011), DAgger — compounding-error argument
  every IL thesis needs.

**2. Modern imitation learning architectures**

- Zhao et al. (RSS 2023), ACT / ALOHA — action chunking; the direct
  ancestor of today's VLA action heads.
- Chi et al. (RSS 2023), Diffusion Policy — generative action heads.
- Lipman et al. (ICLR 2023), Flow Matching — theory behind π0-style
  and GR00T-style flow action heads.
- Fu, Zhao, Finn (2024), Mobile ALOHA — the closest published setup
  to this thesis: whole-body IL on a mobile manipulator.

**3. Vision-language-action models**

- Brohan et al., RT-1 (2022) and RT-2 (2023) — the VLA lineage.
- Open X-Embodiment collaboration (2023/24) — cross-embodiment
  pretraining; why adapting a generalist to OARbot is plausible at all.
- Octo Model Team (2024) — open generalist policy.
- Kim et al. (2024), OpenVLA — open 7B VLA + fine-tuning recipes
  (see also the OpenVLA-OFT follow-up on efficient fine-tuning).
- Black et al. (2024), π0; Physical Intelligence (2025), π0.5 — flow
  matching VLA, open weights via openpi.
- Hugging Face (2025), SmolVLA — small (~450M) VLA designed for
  exactly this compute class; likely the workhorse baseline.
- NVIDIA (2025), GR00T N1 paper (+ N1.5 release notes) — the primary
  model; its dual-system architecture and new-embodiment fine-tuning
  story are directly load-bearing.
- Google DeepMind (2025), Gemini Robotics — closed, but frames the
  state of the art in Background.

**4. Mobile manipulation and assistive context**

- TidyBot (2023), HomeRobot/OVMM (2023), BEHAVIOR-1K (2023) —
  mobile-manipulation task framing and benchmarks.
- RPI's own OARbot publications — get the list from the advisor; the
  assistive-robotics motivation should cite the lab's line of work.

**5. Datasets and evaluation methodology**

- DROID (2024), BridgeData V2 (2023), AgiBot World (2025) —
  large-scale teleop dataset practice worth imitating at small scale.
- LIBERO (2023) — task-suite design and eval discipline.
- SimplerEnv — Li et al. (2024), *Evaluating Real-World Robot
  Manipulation Policies in Simulation* — the real-vs-sim eval gap.
- Recent work on statistically sound robot policy evaluation (trial
  counts, confidence intervals, A/B protocols) — good target for a
  deep-research sweep, see below.

## Open-source stack

| Resource | Use here |
|---|---|
| [LeRobot](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot) | Dataset format, teleop recording, SmolVLA + π0 (PyTorch) training/eval — the backbone of B2/C2 |
| [Isaac GR00T](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Isaac-GR00T) | GR00T N1.5 checkpoints + new-embodiment fine-tuning scripts; check NVIDIA's DGX Spark playbook |
| [openpi](https://github.com/Physical-Intelligence/openpi) | π0/π0.5 reference implementation (JAX) if the LeRobot port falls short |
| [oarbots repo](https://github.com/rpirobotics/oarbots) | Lab's ROS 2 stack, drivers, teleop — extend, don't rewrite |
| Hugging Face Hub | Host the OARbot demonstration dataset (private repo) + fine-tuned checkpoints; free provenance and versioning |
| Weights & Biases (or TensorBoard) | Training curves + eval run tracking, linked from weekly updates |
| Zotero → `references.bib` | Single bibliography pipeline into Quarto |

Stretch only (explicitly out of scope unless everything lands early):
Isaac Lab / SimplerEnv-style sim twin of a task for cheap eval — you
have Isaac Sim experience from the SO-101 project, but a sim twin is
a second thesis; park it in Future Work.

## Using AI research assistants

Division of labor — each tool where it is strongest:

- **Gemini Deep Research** — breadth: one report per Background
  section above ("annotated bibliography of VLA fine-tuning on novel
  embodiments 2023–2026, with arXiv links"). Also the eval-methodology
  sweep in §5.
- **ChatGPT (deep research)** — cross-check Gemini's reports;
  protocol questions ("how many trials for a detectable 15-point
  success-rate difference between two policies?").
- **NotebookLM** — load the collected PDFs per chapter section; ask
  grounded cross-paper questions while writing Background.
- **Claude Code** — everything in-repo: LeRobot/GR00T pipeline code,
  QC scripts, eval analysis, figures, Quarto chapter drafting, and
  keeping this PM surface honest.

Standing rule: LLM output is a *lead*, never a *citation*. Every
claim that survives into the thesis gets verified against the primary
source, and every reference is checked on arXiv before entering
`references.bib`.

## Risk register

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Bring-up eats October (drivers, arm, cameras) | High | Gate 1 fallback: arm-only task suite, decided Sep 26 |
| Demo data too little/noisy for T3 | Medium | Tiered tasks — T1/T2 alone still answer RQ1–RQ3; data-scale ablation turns "not enough data" into a finding |
| GR00T new-embodiment head underperforms | Medium | SmolVLA is the guaranteed baseline; a negative GR00T result, carefully analyzed, is still a thesis result |
| Eval time underestimated | High | Protocol fixed in Sept; ≥20 trials budgeted on the calendar, not squeezed in |
| Generalization round balloons eval time | Medium | Tiers only on best checkpoints, 10 trials/tier; if squeezed, run G1–G4 on T1+T2 only |
| Two-robot temptation (multi-robot experiments) | Medium | One OARbot is the experiment platform; the second is spare parts / backup until the freeze |
| Writing starts late | Medium | Section D outline bar in December; Methods accretes from epic READMEs all semester |

## Cadence

Weekly update (`.\thesis.ps1 new wu`) every Friday: progress, frozen
Gantt snapshot, blockers, questions for advisor. The board and Gantt
on the [home page](../../index.qmd) stay the single source of truth —
no parallel tracker (Notion/Trello) gets created.
